analysis_md:
# BEKE — KE Holdings Inc. (Beike)
v5 run, 2026-10-15. Form 20-F filer (CIK 1809587); price $17.83 per ADS (nasdaq_quote_api). **ADS ratio 3.0 applied** — one ADS represents three Class A ordinary shares (see OVERRIDE / ADS section); all per-share figures below are per ADS unless noted.

Scope note: the engine's market_cap_est ($61.9B) multiplies the ordinary-share count by the per-ADS price, so it overstates the ADS-basis market cap by the 3x ratio; judgment.json therefore carries in_scope_under_40b as the engine computes it, while on an ADS basis the company sits at roughly one-third of that estimate, inside the <$40B sweep scope it was queued from.

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, or cited search results — none are recomputed.

## What it is
China's leading integrated online and offline platform for housing transactions and services ("Beike"), built around the Lianjia brokerage brand and the ACN agent-cooperation network that lets competing brokerages share listings and split commissions. Segments: existing-home transactions, new-home transactions, home renovation and furnishing, and home rental services (Carefree Rent). Q2 2026 (company release via GlobeNewswire): GTV RMB933.8B (+6.3% YoY), net revenues RMB24.5B (−5.7% YoY), net income RMB2,624M (+100.8% YoY), 60,274 stores and 540,634 agents. Q1 2026 was much weaker: revenues −19.0% YoY, new-home GTV −37.2% YoY, profit up only through cost cuts. The profit story in 2026 is margin/cost restructuring, not demand recovery — China's housing market remains in a multi-year downturn.

## Owner's earnings
From financials_history.csv (USD; CNY converted — see FLAGS):
- **FY2025:** OCF −$53,794,000; capex $86,904,000 (PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets); SBC $272,401,000 (always a real cost). **Conservative OE −$413,099,000 = −$0.36/ADS** (base_oe_latest_per_share). Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): −$458,187,000 — same negative ballpark, so the negative year is not a definition artifact. Net income stayed positive at $428,132,000; the OCF leg collapsed instead (see NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE below).
- **FY2024:** OCF $1,294,255,000; capex $142,093,000; SBC $373,471,000; conservative OE $778,691,000. **FY2023:** OCF $1,571,522,000; capex $123,099,000; SBC $452,901,000; conservative OE $995,522,000.
- OE positive 4 of the last 5 fiscal years. Balance sheet is a net-cash position: net debt −$1,085,422,136 (dcf_numbers.json), net debt −0.47x normalized OE — no solvency issue; the question is earnings power, not survival.
- **Base used = normalized median of the last 3 FY OE/share: $0.66/ADS** (base_oe_normalized_per_share $0.6604; base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). The latest FY is negative, so the median is doing real work here — it is the FY2024-level year of the last three. A TTM base could not be used (see STALE_FY below).

## Moat: 6/10 — moderate, real network effects inside a brutal macro
Justification: Beike/Lianjia is China's dominant integrated online-offline housing platform: the ACN agent-cooperation network, the largest verified listing database, the Lianjia brand and ~60k-store / ~540k-agent scale (Q2 2026 release) create real network effects and data advantages rivals cannot quickly replicate. But the moat is narrow-to-moderate, not wide: demand is hostage to China's housing cycle and policy, agents and consumers can multi-home, take rates face regulatory and developer pressure, and the newer renovation/rental lines carry structurally lower margins — earnings power has swung from strong profits to a negative-OE year within the last 3 fiscal years.
- FOR: ACN agent-cooperation network — shared listings/commission splits across ~60k stores and ~540k agents (Q2 2026), scale rivals cannot quickly replicate; largest verified housing listing database + Lianjia brand trust in a fraud-prone resale market; data/AI tooling and transaction infrastructure (VR tours, escrow, closing services) raise agent productivity and platform stickiness; dominant share of existing-home transactions in tier-1/2 cities — existing-home GTV +8.0% YoY in Q2 2026 even in a weak market.
- AGAINST: earnings hostage to China's housing cycle and housing policy — FY2025 operating cash flow went negative; agents and consumers can multi-home, and competing platforms plus developer direct-sales channels pressure take rates; new-home segment tied to distressed developer volumes (Q1 2026 new-home GTV −37.2% YoY); growth lines (renovation, rental) are lower-margin and working-capital heavier than the core brokerage platform; China/VIE/ADS regulatory overhang and Class B weighted-voting governance concentration.
- A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 9.8 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-15)
Engine blended growth g_base 6.55% (components: rev CAGR 5y 4.60%, rev CAGR 3y 15.42%, latest rev YoY 5.63%; share-count trend −0.92%/yr adds +0.92pp — buybacks are real here, ~$195M repurchased in Q1 2026 alone per the Q1 release). Default offsets (−12/−5/0/+5/+12pp) and default OE multipliers (0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25) kept; probabilities skewed bearish (15/30/30/17/8) because OE is volatile, FY2025 OE was negative, and 2026 revenue prints are negative YoY.

**Sanity check vs recent prints:** the base start (+6.55% OE growth) sits above current revenue prints (Q1 2026 −19.0%, Q2 2026 −5.7% YoY) but below Q2's profit trajectory (net income +100.8% YoY on cost cuts; GTV +6.3% YoY) — OE can grow off the trough faster than revenue while restructuring holds. The super-bull start (+18.55%) is an OE-recovery rate off a depressed base, not a revenue claim; it requires a housing stabilization the company has not yet printed — hence only 8% weight. Bear (−5.45% super bear / +1.55% bear starts) matches the Q1 2026 tape if the downturn deepens.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | −5.45% | 0.75 | Housing downturn deepens; FY2025-style OCF weakness repeats | $2.85 | 4.26% |
| Bear | 30% | +1.55% | 0.90 | Market stays flat-to-down; cost cuts only defend margins | $4.67 | 5.74% |
| Base | 30% | +6.55% | 1.00 | Gradual stabilization; OE grows off the normalized base | $6.48 | 7.22% |
| Bull | 17% | +11.55% | 1.10 | Existing-home recovery + rental/renovation scale-up | $8.91 | 9.12% |
| Super bull | 8% | +18.55% | 1.25 | Real housing upcycle; platform operating leverage returns | $13.79 | 12.54% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $6.39/ADS (−64.2% vs the $17.83 price), IV@12% $8.55, IV@10% $10.96, weighted IRR 7.20%, base-case IRR 7.22%.**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Diagnostics: OE yield 3.70%, terminal value 19.4% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.83x, net debt −0.47x normalized OE, 9.5 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9.5 months ago): ttm.py was run and **failed** — "ttm.py: cannot compute TTM for BEKE (CIK 1809587): ocf: no annual (FY) fact; sbc: no annual (FY) fact; shares_diluted: no annual (FY) fact; capex: no capex facts in companyfacts under any candidate tag and no capex_override in judgment.json — refusing to zero-fill". The engine's annual history reads BEKE's filed USD-translation facts that ttm.py's leg-matching does not pick up, so no TTM pin exists. Per spec the engine's normalized median base ($0.66/ADS) is used instead. The 2026 interim prints were still checked qualitatively: Q1 2026 operating cash outflow of RMB1.5B was attributed by the CFO (Q1 earnings call) to timing of accrued employee-compensation payments, and Q2 2026 operating cash flow was reported at RMB6.61B with net income +100.8% YoY — consistent with a volatile-but-not-broken cash engine, and with keeping the median base rather than the negative FY2025 year.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY OE/share −$0.36 vs 3-yr median $0.66): the **latest FY is the distorted one** — FY2025 net income was positive ($428,132,000) while OCF collapsed to −$53,794,000 on working-capital absorption (ΔNWC +$932,992,000 in financials_history.csv) in a weak housing year. The median is retained as the base; the divergence is cyclicality + WC timing, not a restatement.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3x over 5 years): real — this is a housing-cycle business (conservative OE: FY2023 $995,522,000 → FY2025 −$413,099,000). Handled by the normalized median base plus bear-skewed probabilities (45% on bear-or-worse).
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2023, 2024, 2025): identified per year from financials_history.csv. In 2023–2024 OCF ran far **above** net income (2023: OCF $1,571,522,000 vs NI $828,636,000; 2024: $1,294,255,000 vs $556,891,000) — the gap is the non-cash SBC addback (SBC $452,901,000 in 2023, $373,471,000 in 2024, expensed in NI but added back in OCF) plus working-capital release (ΔNWC −$1,074,477,000 in 2023). In 2025 the sign flipped: ΔNWC +$932,992,000 absorbed cash and drove OCF negative despite positive NI. No single one-off tax/impairment item is named in the computed outputs; the divergence is SBC addbacks + WC swings in both directions. The OCF-based conservative OE used throughout already nets SBC out, so the base is not contaminated by the addback side.
- **FX_CONVERTED**: BEKE reports in CNY; the engine converted CNY facts to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — rates recorded in dcf_numbers.json (2024-12-31: 0.137; 2025-12-31: 0.14284 USD per CNY). Flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average — a documented simplification that adds translation noise to year-over-year comparisons.
- **USD_TRANSLATIONS_USED**: for periods where the issuer files its own USD convenience translations, the engine used the filed USD figures as-is; the base rests partly on those issuer translations and partly on the ECB conversions above.
- **ADS_RATIO_APPLIED**: judgment.json declares ads_ratio {ratio: 3.0} under the bounded authority — the ratio is stated in the filer's own Form 20-F (Exhibit 2.5, Description of Rights of Each Class of Securities: ADSs each representing three Class A ordinary shares, NYSE-listed; restated in the company's 2026 SEC filings). Per-share figures were scaled x3 so they are comparable to the $17.83 ADS price; without it the preliminary run compared per-ordinary-share OE to a per-ADS price and understated OE yield 3-fold.
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (engine labels the name Finance): the label is wrong for the actual business — Beike is a real-estate transaction-services platform with no loan book, no insurance float and no deposit funding, so the OCF − capex − SBC model applies to it far better than to a lender. The flag is still honored as instructed: confidence is **low** and no tier upgrade is taken from the model. (If anything the real model risk here is housing cyclicality, covered under OE_VOLATILE.)
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 4.83x super-bear IV): real — outcomes hinge on China's housing path. Confidence capped at low; the verdict is sized to the conservative end. Notably, the spread does not rescue the stock: even the widest end (super bull, $13.79 IV@15, 12.54% IRR) sits below the current price and below the 15% hurdle.

## Thoughts / overlay
- **Method range:** there is no defensible input range spanning the hurdle here. On the normalized median base, every scenario — including super bull at 1.25x OE and +18.55% growth start — returns less than 15% at $17.83. Using the latest-FY base instead would be worse (it is negative; no DCF at all). The bull case for BEKE at this price is a balance-sheet/multiple story (net cash, buybacks, cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments of RMB53.9 billion per the Q1 2026 release — a cited search-result figure, not recomputed) and a housing-recovery option, not an owner's-earnings story.
- **Hurdle-clearing price:** the weighted IV@15% is **$6.39/ADS** — the price at which the weighted path clears 15% before any margin of safety. With a margin of safety for China/VIE and cycle risk, an entry would need to be below that.
- What would change the verdict: two consecutive years of positive conservative OE at or above the FY2023–24 level (proving FY2025 was the trough, not the new run-rate), which would lift both the median base and the OE yield at any given price.

## Verdict
**Tier D (weighted IRR 7.20%, IV@15% $6.39/ADS vs $17.83 price).** A genuinely strong franchise — China's dominant housing platform, moat 6/10, net cash, heavy buybacks — priced far above what its normalized owner's earnings can support: the weighted IV@15% sits 64.2% below the price (upside_at_15 −64.2%), and not even the super-bull scenario clears Andrew's 15% hurdle. Confidence low (sector-model flag honored, wide scenario spread, FX-translated base). No tier override.
